title: Linearization is left adjoint to transport
statement:
Let $P\dashv S$ be an adjunction with $S$ strong monoidal that satisfies the projection
formula, with the projection formula of [def-sfb-adjunction-projection-formula], and let
$\mathcal B$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal D$. Then the linearization
$P_{\mathcal B}$ ([def-sfb-modobj-linearization]) is left adjoint to transport along $S$
([def-sfb-modobj-transport]):
$$
P_{\mathcal B}\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(S)\colon\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D)\to\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C).
$$
A $\mathcal B$-linear map $PM\to N$ corresponds to the $S\mathcal B$-linear adjoint map
$M\to SN$.

proof.text: Write $u:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to SP$ and $c:PS\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ for the unit and counit. By [def-sfb-adjunction-projection-formula], the canonical maps $\pi_{L,M}$ form a projection formula, so [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint] applies with $G=S$. It constructs a right linearization $S_{\mathcal B}$ whose structural map $\theta_{L,N}:SL\otimes SN\to S(L\otimes N)$ is the adjoint of $(L\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{L,SN}$.

source.place: Unit sk-def-sfb-transport, clause 4; specialization G=S in the imported proof

proof.text:
The defining mate of $\pi_{L,SN}$ in [def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula] is $S(\pi_{L,SN})\circ u_{SL\otimes SN}=\mu^S_{L,PSN}\circ(SL\otimes u_{SN})$. Hence, using the definition of $\theta$ from [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint],
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta_{L,N}&=S(L\otimes c_N)\circ S(\pi_{L,SN})\circ u_{SL\otimes SN}\\
&=S(L\otimes c_N)\circ\mu^S_{L,PSN}\circ(SL\otimes u_{SN})\\
&=\mu^S_{L,N}\circ(SL\otimes(Sc_N\circ u_{SN}))
=\mu^S_{L,N}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third equality is naturality of the lax structure map in its second variable for $c_N:PSN\to N$; the last is the adjunction triangle identity $Sc_N\circ u_{SN}=\mathrm{id}_{SN}$. Thus this is an explicit calculation from the definitions and the adjunction axioms, with all maps having source $SL\otimes SN$ and target $S(L\otimes N)$.

source.place: Unit clause 4, identity G_B=mapMod(S); expansion of the imported proof theta=mu calculation

proof.text: For a $\mathcal B$-module object $N$ with action $\gamma_N$, [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint] defines the action on $S_{\mathcal B}N$ as $S\gamma_N\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}$. Step 2 identifies this with $S\gamma_N\circ\mu^S_{\mathcal B,N}$, exactly the action on $\operatorname{mapMod}(S)N$ in [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Both functors send a module morphism $f$ to $Sf$, by those same statements. Thus they agree on module objects and module morphisms, giving the canonical identification $S_{\mathcal B}=\operatorname{mapMod}(S)$.

Apply [def-sfb-modobj-linearized-adjunction] to the projection formula and the adjunction $P\dashv S$ fixed in step 1. It gives $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv S_{\mathcal B}$, where its left functor is the linearization of [def-sfb-modobj-linearization]. Substituting the identification of step 3 gives $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(S)$. The cited adjunction is defined by restricting the original adjunction bijection, so, for every $M\in\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C)$ and $N\in\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D)$, a $\mathcal B$-linear map $PM\to N$ corresponds to its original adjoint $M\to SN$, and this map is $S\mathcal B$-linear for the transport action. This also proves the last clause of the item, with the naturality supplied by the cited adjunction.
